name: Congenital Anomaly of the Great Veins

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Great Vein Anomaly Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal anatomical configuration of the superior or inferior vena cava or pulmonary veins confirmed by imaging
Clinical signs of venous congestion or cyanosis related to anomalous venous return
Echocardiographic evidence of abnormal venous drainage or flow patterns
Exclusion of other major congenital cardiac malformations that could explain symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least two major criteria including anomalous vein structure and clinical signs or imaging confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging modalities such as echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cyanosis due to anomalous venous return
searchTerms: bluish skin from abnormal vein flow
cyanosis from vein blood returning incorrectly

pathognomonic.symptomName: Venous congestion with upper body edema

common.symptomName: Murmur due to turbulent venous flow
searchTerms: heart murmur from abnormal vein flow
noise from turbulent blood in veins
neurological symptoms due to lack of oxygen

rare.symptomName: Arrhythmias secondary to abnormal venous return
searchTerms: arrhythmia caused by abnormal vein return
heart rhythm problems due to vein issues

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes secondary to congestion
imaging: CT angiography or MRI confirming abnormal great vein anatomy
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly or pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with syndromic conditions
other: Physical examination revealing cyanosis and venous congestion signs

distinguishingFeatures: Complete anomalous pulmonary venous drainage with obligatory atrial septal defect
More severe cyanosis and heart failure in neonates
Usually acquired obstruction rather than congenital anomaly
Presence of collateral venous circulation and associated malignancy or thrombosis

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Progressive respiratory distress with poor feeding
